conventions: te ... kai rendered *and also* is two written English words, so rule 70's two-conjunction arm applies and each particle keeps one: te takes *and*, kai takes *also* (2:9, 2:10). Rule 70's word *conjunction* is read as a count of the English words the ASV wrote and not as a part-of-speech test, the corpus's `unrepresented` te units being those where the ASV wrote a single *and* for the pair. ROM.1.16 reads the identical Ioudaioi te proton kai Helleni -> *to the Jew first and also to the Greek* the same way. Emptying te and giving *and also* whole to kai remains defensible.

A postnominal attributive article whose modifier is a participle rendered as a finite clause is `unrepresented`: rule 31 leaves the supplied relativizer with the participle, and where the ASV writes no determiner for the expressed head noun the article has nothing left to carry, so rule 23 empties it. anthropou tou katergazomenou -> *of man that worketh* (2:9) and ethne ta me nomon echonta -> *Gentiles that have not the law* (2:14) are both read this way. Rule 31's clause giving a following article only *which* reaches a verbless modifier, not a participle, and rule 32's apposition clause reaches the same answer, the expressed noun having already written what the relative clause is predicated of. A reference comparison reports both articles as disagreements, and that report is not a correction. An expressed appositional predicate noun is the contrast and is rule 92's case, not this one: 2:27's ton ... parabaten gives the article only the supplied *a* and leaves *who art ... transgressor* to the noun.

en toi phaneroi and en toi kryptoi rendered by a single English word are one `aligned` unit of preposition plus adjective headed on the adjective, with the intervening article `unrepresented` under rule 93 (2:28 twice, 2:29). Rule 93's pleonastic arm is scoped to a governed adverb, and a substantival adjective does not spell an English adverb by itself: the adverbial force of *outwardly* and *inwardly* is what en and the dative contribute, so rule 94's count test joins the pair and rule 39 keeps it `aligned`. The adjectival *outward* at 2:28 is analysed the same way under rule 24 rather than as a pleonastic en with the adjective taking the word alone, which remains defensible for that occurrence alone.
report: Checked all 42 candidate lemma groups and read the 29-verse dump end to end for the asymmetry the table is blind to (a supplied word marked `added` in one verse and folded onto a licensing token in another). No genuine cross-verse split found, so patches is empty.

te ... kai at 2:9 and 2:10 was the one live question, and the evidence settles it. ROM.1.16 carries the identical collocation Ioudaioi te proton kai Helleni -> *to the Jew first and also to the Greek* and reads it exactly as this chapter does: te -> *and*, kai -> *also*, each its own `aligned` unit under rule 70's two-word arm. The corpus's 29 `unrepresented` te units are the other arm; every one whose note is visible (2CO.12.12, ACT.13.1, ACT.15.9) describes the ASV writing a single *and* for the pair. Recorded as a convention. 2:19's te with no answering kai -> *and* is the ordinary case (1CO.4.21, ACT.1.15).

Every other difference in the table is licensed by the source or by what the ASV wrote, not by two analyses. The article groups turn on rule 102's own test: 2:6 anarthrous hekastoi -> *to every man* takes all three words, while 2:10 articular panti toi splits *to every* / *man*, exactly as ROM.1.16 splits *to every* / *one*. So too anarthrous nomou -> *of the law* whole (2:13, 2:25, 2:27) against articular tou nomou -> *of the* / *law* (2:14, 2:15, 2:23, 2:26), and 2:20's *of knowledge* against *of the truth*, which rule 21 decides by the presence of an English determiner and which that verse's own note already argues.

The two postnominal articles standing before participles agree with each other: 2:9 anthropou tou katergazomenou and 2:14 ethne ta me ... echonta are both `unrepresented`, both were corrected during the verse pass, and both leave the relativizer on the participle under rule 31. 2:27's ton ... parabaten -> *a* is a different configuration, an expressed appositional predicate noun, which rule 92 says in terms the rule 31 carve-out does not reach; it is not a third reading of one construction. Recorded as a convention because the competing reading was written twice before correction.

The three en toi phaneroi / en toi kryptoi units (2:28 twice, 2:29) agree: preposition and adjective joined as one `aligned` unit headed on the adjective, article `unrepresented` under rule 93. Rule 93 scopes its pleonastic arm to a governed adverb and does not name an adjective, so this is a chapter judgment rather than a bare application; recorded as a convention with the competing reading for the adjectival *outward* named.

Substantival adjectives (2:9, 2:10, 2:19, 2:20) all take their own supplied determiner under rule 58, matching ROM.1.16's Ioudaioi -> *to the Jew* and Helleni -> *to the Greek*. Supplied possessives divide cleanly and consistently: article `unrepresented` wherever a possessor token stands (2:4, 2:5, 2:6, 2:15, 2:16, 2:25, 2:26, 2:29), article aligned under rule 20's second arm wherever none does (2:15 ton -> *their*, 2:18 to -> *his*, 2:23 tes -> *thy*).

BSB: none of the six disagreements is an error. 2:1 ton (bare *another*, no determiner written) and 2:24 tou / 2:4 tes are rules 23 and 20 as written; 2:28 toi is rule 93; 2:9 tou and 2:14 ta are the rule 31 reading above, which those verses' notes already flag as a report that is not a correction. The 98.4% figure should not be read as movable here.

The chapter has exactly one `added` unit, the supplied rhetorical *not* at 2:27, and no comparable supplied negation is folded anywhere else, so the table's blind spot holds nothing. The italicized *shall be* at 2:8, *them* at 2:15, *a man should* at 2:21 and 2:22, *if it* at 2:27 and *one* at 2:28 and 2:29 are each folded onto a token that licenses them, and the two *one* units agree with each other.

No promotion offered. The strongest candidate was amending rule 70's *two English conjunctions* to a count of the English words the ASV wrote, which would settle *and also* for the whole testament; confirming it needs the 29 `unrepresented` te units read individually to be sure none of them is an *and also*, and this run's single evidence round returned the aggregate rather than that subset. A later chapter carrying te ... kai can ask for LEMMA=te STATUS=unrepresented and promote it. Until then the judgment is recorded as a ROM.2 convention only.

One cosmetic point for a later reader rather than a patch: 2:18's ek -> *out of* cites rule 106, but no compound verb stands there (katechoumenos is not an ek- compound); the edge is right under rule 36 as an ordinary two-word English preposition, and the citation is the only thing loose about it.
